sop_modules.name: Foundation Protection Setup
sop_modules.description: Deploy landscape perimeter protection and hardscape covers adjacent to foundation wall. Foundation is a LOW protection spec — ground-level work with limited overspray risk. Siding/trim protection above foundation is NOT this spec's responsibility.

tasks.name: Landscape Perimeter Protection
tasks.description: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting along foundation perimeter where landscape (plantings, mulch, soil) is adjacent to foundation wall. Measured in linear feet along foundation base. Full cover for spray (overspray drift at ground level), edge tarps for roll/brush.

quality_notes.all: Secure tarps against wind with stakes or weights. UV-resistant 4 mil plastic minimum. Cover plantings within spray drift zone when spraying.

tasks.name: Walkway Protection
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths and plastic over walkways adjacent to foundation wall. Conditional — only when walkway is adjacent to working elevation.

quality_notes.all: Canvas for crew traffic areas (non-slip). Plastic for spray protection. Tape plastic to foundation edge at grade line.

tasks.name: Patio Protection
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths and plastic over patio surfaces adjacent to foundation wall. Conditional — only when patio is adjacent to working elevation.

quality_notes.all: Full cover for spray. Edge tarps for roll/brush. Protect patio furniture if present.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Landscape protection first -> Hardscape walk/patio protection (if adjacent).

sop_modules.name: Foundation Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: NC foundation prep: moisture testing (MC <= 4% HARD STOP — stricter than masonry wall 12%), form-release/laitance removal (poured concrete only), efflorescence treatment (if present), pressure wash, crack patching, bug hole patching (poured only), surface profiling. CRITICAL: NEVER caulk the 3/8-inch siding-to-foundation gap — it is an intentional drainage plane. Mask the gap, do not seal it.

tasks.name: Moisture Content Testing
tasks.description: Test moisture content of foundation wall surface with electronic moisture meter at multiple points across the above-grade band. Must read MC <= 4% before any coating application. This is a HARD STOP — do NOT coat if MC exceeds 4%. Foundation MC limit is stricter than masonry wall (12%) due to continuous ground contact and capillary moisture rise.

quality_notes.QT2: Spot check representative areas on each working elevation.
quality_notes.QT3: Check multiple points per elevation. Document all readings. Every area must pass MC <= 4%.

tasks.name: Form-Release Agent & Laitance Removal
tasks.description: Remove waxy/oily form-release agents and weak laitance layer from poured concrete foundation surface. These bond-breakers prevent coating adhesion — coating applied over form-release agents will peel off in sheets within weeks. Methods: wire brush/mechanical abrasion, chemical detergent, or pressure wash with TSP. Water bead test: splash water on surface — if water beads, form-release agent is still present. Poured concrete ONLY — not applicable to CMU.

quality_notes.all: Water bead test after removal: splash water on cleaned surface. Water should absorb, not bead. If water beads, continue removal. Verify adhesion with tape test on small area before full application.

tasks.name: Efflorescence Treatment
tasks.description: Remove efflorescence (white salt deposits) before any coating. Coating over active efflorescence causes osmotic blistering — salts migrate through the coating creating pressure bubbles. Treatment: (1) dry brush for light deposits, (2) TSP wash for moderate, (3) phosphoric acid for severe (unlikely on NC foundation). Conditional — only when efflorescence is present.

quality_notes.QT2: Brush off loose efflorescence. Water wash.
quality_notes.QT3: Full removal with TSP if moderate. Verify moisture source addressed. Re-test MC after treatment.

tasks.name: Pressure Wash Foundation
tasks.description: Pressure wash foundation wall to remove construction dust, dirt, debris, and loose material. Use 1,500-2,500 PSI — sufficient for concrete/CMU cleaning without surface damage. Allow 24-48 hr dry time before coating. Re-verify MC <= 4% after drying.

quality_notes.QT2: Basic water wash to remove visible dirt and debris.
quality_notes.QT3: Full pressure wash with TSP solution. Rinse thoroughly. Allow 24-48 hr dry time. Re-check MC <= 4%.

tasks.name: Cosmetic Crack Patching
tasks.description: Patch cosmetic cracks less than 1/8 inch wide in foundation wall. Use masonry patching compound. Cracks wider than 1/8 inch indicate potential structural issues — refer to GC/structural engineer, not painting contractor scope.

quality_notes.all: Fill and smooth cracks to match surrounding surface. Allow patch to cure before coating. Cracks >1/8 inch = STOP and report to GC.

tasks.name: Bug Hole & Form-Tie Patching
tasks.description: Fill bug holes (small air voids) and form-tie penetrations in poured concrete foundation with hydraulic cement. These are casting artifacts unique to poured concrete. Poured concrete ONLY — not applicable to CMU.

quality_notes.all: Fill completely and smooth flush with surrounding surface. Hydraulic cement for form-tie holes. Allow full cure before coating.

tasks.name: Surface Profile Check & Correction
tasks.description: Verify Concrete Surface Profile (CSP) matches intended coating thickness. For above-grade cosmetic coating (<10 mils DFT), CSP 1-2 is appropriate. If surface is too smooth (laitance present) or too rough, correct with light mechanical abrasion. 83% of foundation coating failures originate from insufficient surface roughness.

quality_notes.all: CSP 1-2 target for thin cosmetic coating. If surface is glassy smooth (laitance), light abrade to open pores. If too rough (CSP 3+), no correction needed — cosmetic coating fills minor texture.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Moisture test (HARD STOP if MC >4%) -> Form-release removal (poured only) -> Efflorescence treatment (if present) -> Pressure wash -> Dry time (24-48 hr) -> Re-verify MC <= 4% -> Crack patching -> Bug hole/form-tie patching (poured only) -> Surface profile check.
critical_warnings: NEVER caulk the 3/8-inch siding-to-foundation gap. It is an intentional drainage plane with Z-flashing. Caulking causes catastrophic moisture damage to siding and sheathing. MASK the gap during painting.
MC <= 4% is a HARD STOP. Do NOT proceed if moisture content exceeds 4%. Foundation walls have continuous ground contact — capillary moisture rise is expected. Test, wait, re-test.
Oil-based and alkyd products are PROHIBITED on alkaline concrete/CMU. Saponification is catastrophic and irreversible.

sop_modules.name: CMU Block Filler Application
sop_modules.description: Apply block filler (PCA P12 Level 2 Standard Fill) to CMU foundation surfaces. Fills open-cell voids. This is substrate preparation — NOT primer. Applied BEFORE alkali-resistant primer. CMU ONLY — not needed on poured concrete. Material system: SYS_EXT_FNDN_BLOCK_FILLER.

tasks.name: Block Filler — Spray Application
tasks.description: Apply block filler by airless spray (527-535 tip, 30-mesh filter, 2,300-3,000 PSI). On CMU foundation, spray SHOULD be followed by backroll to force filler into voids per masonry doctrine. Single coat. Material system: SYS_EXT_FNDN_BLOCK_FILLER.

quality_notes.all: Back-roll IMMEDIATELY while filler is wet. Force filler into all voids. No holidays or unfilled voids. Verify PCA P12 Level 2 standard: max 10 voids per SF after application.

tasks.name: Block Filler — Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply block filler by heavy roller (1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap). Work filler into all voids with heavy nap roller. Multiple passes may be needed. Roll is the typical method for small CMU foundation bands. Single coat. Material system: SYS_EXT_FNDN_BLOCK_FILLER.

quality_notes.all: Heavy pressure to force filler into voids. Multiple passes if needed. Verify all voids filled. PCA P12 Level 2: max 10 voids per SF.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Applied AFTER prep module completes. Applied BEFORE primer module. Allow block filler to cure per product TDS (typically 4-8 hours) before primer application.

sop_modules.name: Alkali-Resistant Foundation Primer
sop_modules.description: Full field prime coat with alkali-resistant primer (rated to pH 13). MANDATORY on ALL new foundation (pH 12-14 when new) regardless of quality tier — this is not quality-optional. Enables 7-day accelerated coating schedule vs 28-day standard cure. Applied over block filler on CMU, directly to bare concrete on poured. Material system: SYS_EXT_FNDN_PRIMER_ALKALI. Oil-based primer is PROHIBITED — saponification on alkaline concrete is catastrophic.

tasks.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer — Spray
tasks.description: Apply alkali-resistant foundation primer by airless spray (517 tip, 60-mesh filter, 1,500-2,500 PSI). Spray-only IS valid for foundation (unlike masonry wall) — smooth poured concrete does not require forced pore penetration. For CMU foundation, consider backroll per masonry doctrine. Single coat.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays or thin spots.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. Inspect for complete coverage. Every pore saturated.

tasks.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer — Roll
tasks.description: Apply alkali-resistant foundation primer by roller (3/4 inch nap for poured concrete, 1-1/4 inch nap for CMU). Work primer into surface pores. Roll is the typical primary method for small foundation bands. Single coat.

quality_notes.all: Work primer into all pores and surface texture. Even coverage. Maintain wet edge. Use appropriate nap: 3/4 inch for smooth poured concrete, 1-1/4 inch for CMU.

tasks.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer — Brush Detail
tasks.description: Apply alkali-resistant primer by brush. Detail work around penetrations (pipes, vents, electrical), tight areas, and edges. Brush is never the primary method for foundation field — supplemental to spray or roll.

quality_notes.all: Work primer into all surface texture around penetrations and edges. Even coverage. Maintain wet edge.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Single prime coat. Applied AFTER block filler on CMU, directly to bare concrete on poured. Allow primer to cure per product TDS before finish coat.

sop_modules.name: Foundation Finish Coat Application
sop_modules.description: Finish coat(s) on primed foundation. Two coating options: (1) Acrylic exterior masonry paint (SYS_EXT_FNDN_FINISH_ACRYLIC) — wider color range, UV-resistant. (2) Cementitious coating/Drylok-type (SYS_EXT_FNDN_FINISH_CEMENTITIOUS) — fills pores, breathable, matte, budget-friendly. QT2 = 1 finish coat (acceptable on properly primed foundation). QT3 = 2 finish coats. No interstage module — QT2/QT3 only, no sanding between coats warranted on utilitarian foundation.

tasks.name: Acrylic Finish — Spray
tasks.description: Apply acrylic exterior masonry finish by airless spray (517 tip, 60-mesh filter). Spray-only IS valid on smooth poured concrete foundation — forced pore penetration not required on cosmetic above-grade coating. Flat sheen. Material system: SYS_EXT_FNDN_FINISH_ACRYLIC.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays. Single coat.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. Two coats — allow recoat time per TDS between coats. No visible pattern at 6 ft.

tasks.name: Acrylic Finish — Roll
tasks.description: Apply acrylic exterior masonry finish by roller (3/4 inch nap for poured concrete, 1-1/4 inch nap for CMU). Roll is the typical primary method for foundation bands. Flat sheen. Material system: SYS_EXT_FNDN_FINISH_ACRYLIC.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. Maintain wet edge. Single coat.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform coverage. Two coats — allow recoat time per TDS. Consistent roller texture.

tasks.name: Cementitious Coating — Roll
tasks.description: Apply cementitious coating (Drylok-type) by roller. Roller is the preferred method for cementitious coatings — thick consistency works well with heavy nap roller. 1-1/4 inch nap. Matte finish. Withstands 15 PSI hydrostatic pressure. Material system: SYS_EXT_FNDN_FINISH_CEMENTITIOUS.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. Work coating into surface pores. Single coat.
quality_notes.QT3: Full coverage. Two coats — allow cure per TDS between coats. Consistent texture.

tasks.name: Cementitious Coating — Brush
tasks.description: Apply cementitious coating (Drylok-type) by brush. Detail work around penetrations and tight areas. Brush provides excellent pore penetration with cementitious products. Material system: SYS_EXT_FNDN_FINISH_CEMENTITIOUS.

quality_notes.all: Work coating into all surface texture. Even coverage. Maintain wet edge. Brush provides good pore penetration for cementitious products.

tasks.name: Finish Coat — Brush Detail/Edges
tasks.description: Brush detail work at penetrations (pipes, vents, electrical conduit), edges, and transitions. Supplemental to spray or roll primary method. Applies to both acrylic and cementitious coatings.

quality_notes.all: Clean transitions at penetrations. No bare spots around pipes/vents. NEVER fill/caulk the siding-to-foundation gap — mask only.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: QT2: Single finish coat on primed surface. QT3: Two finish coats — allow recoat time per product TDS between coats. Acrylic and cementitious are mutually exclusive (selected via coating_type dimension). No interstage sanding — utilitarian surface.

qt_coat_system.QT2: 1 finish coat (single coat acceptable on properly primed foundation)
qt_coat_system.QT3: 2 finish coats (standard residential where foundation appearance matters)

sop_modules.name: Foundation Final Inspection
sop_modules.description: Final walkthrough of completed foundation coating. Inspect all working elevations for coverage consistency, holidays, and defects. Touch up as needed.

tasks.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
tasks.description: Walk all working elevations and inspect finished foundation coating for coverage consistency, holidays, and defects. Foundation is low-visibility utilitarian surface — inspection standard is appropriate to surface importance.

quality_notes.QT2: Quick scan for obvious misses and bare spots.
quality_notes.QT3: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft viewing distance. Check all elevations. Verify clean transition at siding gap (masked, not caulked).

tasks.name: Final Touch-Up
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. Focus on holidays, thin spots, and areas around penetrations.

quality_notes.QT3: Fix all noted defects. Clean edges at transitions.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect all elevations -> Touch up -> Sign off.

sop_modules.name: Foundation Cleanup & Protection Teardown
sop_modules.description: Remove all protection materials, clean equipment, restore site. Foundation is a small scope — quick teardown.

tasks.name: Protection Material Removal
tasks.description: Remove all landscape tarps, hardscape covers, masking tape, and plastic sheeting. Check for overspray on adjacent surfaces. Clean any overspray from hardscape immediately (easier when fresh).

quality_notes.all: Remove all protection materials completely. Inspect landscape for overspray. Clean any hardscape overspray immediately.

tasks.name: Tool & Equipment Cleaning
tasks.description: Clean all application tools. Flush sprayer if used (masonry coatings are abrasive — full flush cycle). Clean roller frames, dispose of saturated covers. Clean brushes. Collect all debris — caulk tubes, tape, plastic, paint cans.

quality_notes.all: Full flush cycle for sprayer if used. Tips and filters cleaned and stored. Site restored to pre-work condition. All materials and debris removed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Protection teardown -> Equipment cleaning -> Site cleanup.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 1 Finish Coat (Poured Concrete, QT2)
round_configurations.description: 1 alkali-resistant primer + 1 finish coat on poured concrete foundation.
round_configurations.notes: QT2 economy. Single finish coat on properly primed surface. Acceptable for utilitarian foundation band.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 2 Finish Coats (Poured Concrete, QT3)
round_configurations.description: 1 alkali-resistant primer + 2 finish coats on poured concrete foundation.
round_configurations.notes: QT3 standard. Two finish coats for higher-end residential where foundation appearance matters. No interstage sanding — utilitarian surface.

round_configurations.name: Block Filler + Prime + 1 Finish Coat (CMU, QT2)
round_configurations.description: 1 block filler + 1 alkali-resistant primer + 1 finish coat on CMU foundation.
round_configurations.notes: QT2 economy CMU. Block filler is phase=prep (substrate preparation, not a coating). 3 total applied layers: filler + primer + 1 finish.

round_configurations.name: Block Filler + Prime + 2 Finish Coats (CMU, QT3)
round_configurations.description: 1 block filler + 1 alkali-resistant primer + 2 finish coats on CMU foundation.
round_configurations.notes: QT3 standard CMU. 4 total applied layers: filler + primer + 2 finish. No interstage sanding.

key_foundation_rules_enforced: MC <= 4% hard stop (stricter than masonry wall 12%) — foundation has continuous ground contact and capillary moisture rise.
NEVER caulk the 3/8-inch siding-to-foundation gap. It is an intentional drainage plane. Mask only.
Oil-based and alkyd products PROHIBITED on all tasks — alkaline concrete/CMU causes saponification.
Alkali-resistant primer MANDATORY on ALL new foundation regardless of quality tier.
Block filler is a separate module BEFORE prime (CMU only).
Spray-only IS valid for foundation (unlike masonry walls) — smooth poured concrete does not require forced pore penetration.
CMU foundation with spray SHOULD include backroll per masonry doctrine.
QT2-QT3 only — foundation is utilitarian, not decorative. No QT4/QT5.
No interstage module — no sanding between coats warranted on utilitarian foundation.
Ground-level access only — no height modifier.

assumptions.value: Spray-only (without mandatory backroll) IS valid for smooth poured concrete foundation
assumptions.note: Unlike masonry wall spec where spray = always spray_backroll, foundation coating on smooth poured concrete does not require forced pore penetration. CMU foundation with spray should still include backroll per masonry doctrine.

assumptions.value: No interstage module — QT2/QT3 only, no intercoat sanding on utilitarian foundation
assumptions.note: Foundation is utilitarian surface. QT4/QT5 excluded. No sanding between finish coats is warranted.

assumptions.value: Efflorescence treatment is a site-condition-gated task (include_when efflorescence_present)
assumptions.note: Same assumption as masonry wall spec. Doctrine describes treatment procedures but does not define efflorescence_present as a formal site_condition_id. Flag for Site_Condition_Vocabulary addition.

assumptions.value: QT2 single finish coat is acceptable on properly primed foundation
assumptions.note: Foundation is utilitarian — single coat on properly primed surface provides adequate protection and appearance for QT2.
